newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--New fines at the Athens Stock Exchange within the week as the Capital Market Commission begins examining reports of more profiteering and speculation.

--With the aim of encouraging cooperation with Greek private investors in major investment programmes, Development Minister Vasso Papandreou yesterday said the government's policy was for the happy co-existence of private and public capital expanding into the Balkans.
--The majority of the working capital of mutual funds in invested in state bonds, according to latest figures.
--Tomorrow's auction will see the premiere of five- and seven-year bonds with interest rates ranging from 8.9-9.8 percent.
IMERISIA

--Domestic investors are readjusting their drachma strategy, preferring short-term high returns in synthetic swaps while the interest of foreign investors in long-term drachma placements appears to be on the wane.
--Tomorrow's auction of long-term bonds will be in effect an evaluation of the progress of interest rates. The finance ministry hopes to raise 300 billion drachmas from the auction.
--The crisis in the Balkans is a passing phase and the region is still there for investors, the vice-president of the European Investment Bank Panayiotis Yennimatas said yesterday.
KERDOS

--This week will see announcements for the posts of managing consultants at most of the 10 public organisations and bodies (DEKOs), including Olympic Airways, Greek Railways, the Athens Water and Sewage Company and Exports Promotion Council.The national economy ministry believes that the selection procedure will have been completed by the beginning of summer.
--The rally at the Athens bourse since the beginning of the year was not enough to take the ASE off the lowest P/E ratio in European markets, according to Investable and Global indices of IFC.

--The Agricultural Bank of Greece has asked the finance ministry to readjust interest rates of short-term bonds received from the state in the framework of expanding its portfolio, according to sources.
EXPRESS
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou insists that there is a need for a "Balkan campaign" with the coordination of private and public investment.
--Developments in shipping are optimistic, following yesterday's meeting between shipowners and Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--The crises Balkan countries are currently going through will work as catharsis and bring better days, most of the speakers at the 4th Congress of Business Cooperation said yesterday in Thessaloniki.
--A further two cooperative banks are awaiting licences from the Bank of Greece. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
